methodology.title: Methodology
methodology.intro: How Forecast Arena collects and combines the forecasts, and where the numbers stop being trustworthy.

sources.title: Sources
sources.body:
Nine numerical models come from the Open-Meteo forecast API and one from MET Norway’s Locationforecast. The models start a new run at 00, 06, 12 and 18 UTC. A city’s forecast is fetched when someone opens it and the stored one is 3 hours old or more, and stored hour by hour, from 3 hours before the run to 320 hours after it.
The charts use 3-hour slots on the city’s local clock (00, 03, 06…), starting at the slot the forecast was fetched in, with a line at the current time: ten days on the landing overview and on the city dashboard. Temperature, wind and pressure are the values at the slot; precipitation is the amount of the 3 hours after it, and hovering a bar selects those 3 hours.
Regional models return data only inside their domain, so a city outside Europe shows up to eight models. MET Norway publishes hourly values for about the first 60 hours only; later slots use the other models.
Feels-like is computed for every model with Open-Meteo’s formula (Steadman’s apparent temperature) from temperature, humidity, wind and sunshine; MET Norway publishes no sunshine, so its feels-like is the value in the shade. Wind gusts come from the nine Open-Meteo models only. Humidity and cloud cover are percentages, charted on their whole range.

median.title: Median and spread
median.body: The median is the middle value of all models that returned data for a step (with an even count, the mean of the two middle values). The dashboard’s bands show the range from the lowest to the highest model and the middle half of the models. Wind direction uses a circular median, so 350° and 10° meet at north. The chance of rain is the share of models forecasting more than {rain} mm in a 3-hour slot (the row under the overview’s precipitation bars).

disagreement.title: Disagreement
disagreement.body: For temperature, wind and pressure the daily disagreement is the average, over the day’s future steps, of the spread between the highest and the lowest model. For precipitation it is the range of the models’ daily totals, each hour counted on the day it ends. Days are in the city’s local time. Thresholds:

limits.title: Limits
limits.body: Model values are grid-point values, not the weather at a street corner; the grid point’s elevation can differ from the city’s, which matters for temperature. Agreement is not accuracy: models that share data or physics can agree and still be wrong together. The models are compared with each other, not with what actually happened: measuring which model has been right is a separate feature planned after the MVP.
